title: Felix and the Tide
premise: Wren Nystrom inherited her late aunt's failing vineyard along with a mountain of debt, and she's spent two years pretending the place—and her heart—are fine. When her estranged family summons her to a reunion where her success will be scrutinized, she hires Felix Marchetti, the charming local carpenter who's been quietly repairing the winery, to pose as her boyfriend. The fake date turns real by dessert, but Felix is hiding his own secret: he's gathering evidence against the developer who swindled his family out of their land—the same developer now circling Wren's vineyard. As foreclosure looms and Felix's investigation endangers them both, Wren must choose between protecting herself and fighting, alongside her found family of vineyard misfits, for justice the courts won't deliver; in the end they expose the developer publicly, save the vineyard as a cooperative, and Wren finally gives her whole heart instead of lending pieces.
about_author: Juniper Montrose is the pen name of a former sommelier who traded tasting rooms for writing nooks on the Oregon coast. Her romances pair stubborn heroines with small towns that refuse to let anyone stay invisible.

chapters.title: Muscle Memory
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Two years after inheriting her aunt's debt-ridden vineyard, Wren runs it like a fortress: precise, guarded, alone. A foreclosure notice arrives the same week as her mother's reunion invitation. She catalogs her heart like inventory—trainable, containable—while secretly drinking wine alone in the cellar. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as control.

chapters.title: The Carpenter's Estimate
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix Marchetti has been patching the winery's rotting porch for months, watching Wren pretend not to need anyone. When she mentions the reunion, he impulsively offers to be her fake boyfriend—he needs a reason to attend the same gala where the Halvorsen Development Group will be honored. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They negotiate rules over cheap wine: no real feelings, no questions about the gala, hand-holding permitted. Wren teaches Felix to taste wine; he teaches her to laugh at herself. Each rule is broken within hours. Emotional beat: playful intimacy that neither will name.

chapters.title: Reunion
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the family estate, Wren performs happiness while her mother catalogues her failures and her brother pushes her to sell the vineyard to Halvorsen. Felix plays her boyfriend flawlessly—too flawlessly. By dessert, dancing under string lights, the performance dissolves into something terrifyingly real, and they kiss. Emotional beat: the mask slips and neither reaches for it.

chapters.title: Morning After Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren wakes panicked, drafting a contract amendment to keep things 'professional.' Felix, guilt-ridden, nearly confesses why he wanted into the gala but can't risk the investigation. Instead he throws himself into restoring the vineyard's old press barn with the winery's ragtag crew—Marta the fermenter, Dee the teenager who never leaves. Emotional beat: found family forming around unspoken secrets.

chapters.title: What Halvorsen Wants
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix reveals fragments: Halvorsen swindled his parents' orchard years ago using forged appraisals, and he's been collecting documents ever since. Now Halvorsen is pressuring Wren's bank to call her loan. When a suspicious 'appraiser' visits the vineyard, Felix recognizes the firm's forged paperwork style. Emotional beat: protective fury hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The whole crew harvests through the night ahead of a storm, and Wren, for the first time, lets people help her. In the dark between rows, Felix tells her everything—his family, the evidence, the risk. Wren realizes staying invisible was never safety; it was just slow loss. Emotional beat: surrender to trust.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Halvorsen escalates: the bank demands full repayment in thirty days, and an anonymous complaint triggers a regulatory audit of the winery. Wren's brother offers a lifeline—if she sells. Felix's key witness recants under pressure. Everything they've built begins collapsing at once. Emotional beat: despair, and the choice to fight anyway.

chapters.title: Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. The crew executes a plan: crash the Halvorsen gala where Felix's documents will be projected before investors, while Marta's testimony and Dee's digital forensics expose the forged appraisals—including the one used on Wren's vineyard. Chaos, confrontation, and Wren publicly claiming the vineyard, the crew, and Felix as hers. Emotional beat: courage as collective act.

chapters.title: First Pressing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Investigations open, Halvorsen's deals unravel, and the bank, shamed, restructures the loan. The vineyard becomes a worker-owned cooperative; Felix's parents visit the restored press barn. On the crush pad, pressing their first co-harvested vintage, Wren admits the heart was never a muscle to contain—it was a door. She opens it all the way. Emotional beat: belonging, earned and chosen.
